bifrost: springboard/src/bare/input.rs (Device, InputSet, Decoder), springboard/src/bare/pointer_finger.rs, springboard/sdk/src/runtime.rs (Input enum)
summary: BifrOSt reads human interface devices through Linux evdev in the system layer. Apps that declare the hid permission can read and write raw reports of one HID device the person picked (the shell reads /dev/hidrawN for them), parse the report descriptor into elements, and match devices by usage; keyboards, keypads and security keys are never offered. Driver authoring is n/a (the kernel owns drivers). Multitouch digitizer data and virtual HID devices for apps remain open.

features.feature: Driver authoring (HIDDriverKit C++ driver classes, system extension packaging)
features.bifrost: none; drivers are Linux kernel drivers
features.note: A user-space driver model for a desktop SDK is not planned; the Linux kernel owns HID drivers

Runs in the shell; apps never open devices. Blocker: Device::open takes an exclusive grab, so an app reader would receive no events, and the shell's decoded keys and touches reach apps through the runtime input enum instead. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): Apps now have an API: with the hid manifest permission and the person's consent for one device, the shell opens /dev/hidrawN (read without grabbing, so the desktop keeps the device), reads input reports on a worker and sends them as report events; output and feature reports go through hid_write, hid_get_feature and hid_set_feature. Keyboards, keypads and FIDO keys are refused outright (hidraw::protected). Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-core usb_grants:: usb_session:: hidraw:: and cargo test -p springboard --features desktop-wayland usb_access::; on the device: plug a gamepad or a vendor HID device, grant it from an app that declares `hid`, and read Event::Report.

features.feature: Device discovery and matching by capability
features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 6 tests. Wave 5 (w5-hiddriverkit, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Matching is by evdev capability, not by HID usage pairs; no app-facing matching API 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): Filters carry the HID usage page and usage, and the service matches them against the top-level collections read from each hidraw device's report descriptor (hidraw::top_level_usages), so an app asks for a device by usage as well as by capability. Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-core usb_grants:: usb_session:: hidraw:: (usb_grants::tests::hid_candidates_are_always_eligible_and_filter_by_usage, hidraw::tests::top_level_usages_find_each_application_collection_once).

features.apple: Handling Keyboard Events from a Human Interface Device, kIOHIDSupportedKeyboardUsagePairsKey
features.bifrost: springboard/src/bare/input.rs:16-18 (Key, Switch events), springboard/sdk/src/runtime.rs:20-28 (Input::Key), springboard/src/bare/key_usage.rs (usage_of, code_of, boot_modifier_bit, boot_report), springboard/core/src/hidraw.rs
features.note: Key events stay evdev codes, and key_usage maps them to HID keyboard usages (page 0x07) with a boot keyboard report and roll-over, tested in springboard/tests/parity_sdk-complete-46.rs. Gap: no keyboard usage-pair declaration is published to the system, and keys outside the boot set (keypad, media, vendor keys) have no usage. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): Raw keyboard reports are never given to apps (the hidraw path refuses keyboard collections), which is the privacy rule for HID input: an app gets keys only through the window system while it has focus. Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-core usb_grants:: usb_session:: hidraw:: (hidraw::tests::keyboards_keypads_and_security_keys_are_protected).

features.bifrost: springboard/src/bare/input.rs:63-65 (protocol B decoder, first contact only), springboard/sdk/src/runtime.rs:21 (Input::Touch)
features.note: Only slot 0 is tracked; no digitizer collection or per-contact data for apps

features.apple: IOHIDDigitizerStylusData, Handling Stylus Input from a Human Interface Device
features.note: Pure model in bifrost_ui::stylus: pressure maps to force, tilt maps to altitude and azimuth, and hover reports are skipped. These mappings are tested headless in springboard/ui/tests/parity_sdk-tests-07-w7.rs. Not wired into apps or the shell and not tested on the VM or Midget. No device decoding; the eraser flag is carried on the report but to_point does not act on it.

features.bifrost: springboard/ui/src/device_match.rs (Criteria::pointer, Capabilities); springboard/src/bare/pointer_finger.rs (Mouse, PointerFinger), springboard/src/bare/input.rs:382 (PointerDecoder), :656 (pointer source selection)
features.note: A pointer device is matched by capability (relative motion and a left button), tested headless in parity_sdk-os-01. Gap: scroll wheel axes are not a matching criterion, and no app reads pointer events.

Lid, tablet mode and headset states, their edges, and per-observer SwitchWatch selection are tested headless in ui/tests/parity_sdk-complete-37.rs. Gap: the shell does not yet publish switch edges to apps, and the feed needs the tablet or Midget hardware.

features.bifrost: springboard/src/bare/input.rs:205-207 (writes a one-finger swipe or tap into an evdev node)
features.note: Only touch gestures are synthesised, for test and automation; no app-facing virtual device API 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): Decision: no app-facing virtual device. Synthetic input stays the shell's events service, gated by the accessibility permission; a uinput device would let an app type as the person with no consent step. Midget check: none; the events service is checked with its existing tests (services::event_services).

features.feature: Raw HID report and element access for apps
features.apple: IOHIDElement, HID Usage Tables, Low-Level Information
features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 7 tests. Wave 2 (theme-18, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No API exposes HID report elements or usage tables to apps 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): usb_access::hid_descriptor parses the report descriptor of an opened device into bifrost_ui::hid_report elements and collections, and an element reads its field out of the payload of an Event::Report by usage. Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-app usb_access:: external_accessory:: usb_printer:: (usb_access::tests::the_report_descriptor_of_an_opened_hid_device_parses_into_elements); on the device the same with a real device's report.

gaps: No app-facing API for HID elements or usage tables; raw reports are read through hidraw nodes (sdk hid_reports.rs)
Stylus and pen data (pressure, tilt, eraser) is not decoded
Touch decoding tracks only the first contact (slot 0)
No app-facing device matching or hotplug notification by HID usage
Synthetic input exists only for touch gestures, with no general virtual HID device API
